{{Short description|Australian mathematician}}
'''Alexander Jason Dunn''' is an Australian mathematician who works in analytic number theory. He has been an assistant professor at the [[Georgia Tech|Georgia Institute of Technology]] since 2023. Previously, he was a postdoc at the [[California Institute of Technology]] for three years, mentored by [[Maksym Radziwill]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sloman |first=Leila |date=2022-08-15 |title=A Numerical Mystery From the 19th Century Finally Gets Solved |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/a-numerical-mystery-from-the-19th-century-finally-gets-solved-20220815/ |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=AJD |url=https://alexjdunn.weebly.com/ |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=AJD |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Dunn - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=262283 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241215104544/https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=262283 |archive-date=2024-12-15 |access-date=2025-07-05 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org |url-status=live }}</ref>

Dunn received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate degree]] in 2020 from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] under the supervision of Scott Ahlgren and [[Alexandru Zaharescu]]. In 2024, he won the [[SASTRA Ramanujan Prize]] in mathematics, citing his "several breakthroughs in the study of modular forms, half-integral weight forms, metaplectic forms and their connections to prime numbers and integer partitions."<ref>{{Cite web |title=SASTRA PRIZE |url=https://www.qseries.org/sastra-prize/ |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=www.qseries.org}}</ref>
